first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this one after the Greece article, so Crete must be on the table now. The opening talks about how many guests, which ceremony and which airport they land at. That's the right order of questions, so I'm reading on. Plain, sensible writing, no gushing.

journey.quote: Exclusive use usually means a chosen space rather than the whole hotel, and curfews and minimum nights are rarely published, so get them in writing before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: Good. 'In writing' and 'before you pay a deposit' in the first few lines. I'd have said exactly that to her.

journey.section: Crete wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Rooms on site | Exclusive use |
journey.reaction: Fifteen rows and six columns, and half of it says 'Not published'. On the iPad I have to pinch and scroll sideways. I'll look at it properly on the computer with my husband.

journey.section: How to compare Crete venues like for like
journey.quote: Rooms matter more than usual when most guests fly long-haul from Australia. Housing them where you marry takes a transfer out of every day of the trip.
journey.reaction: Yes. Mum is not getting in and out of a minibus every morning. Whoever wrote this has thought about the older relatives.

journey.section: How to compare Crete venues like for like
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor asks each venue on your shortlist and confirms these in writing for your date: the curfew, minimum nights, music rules, set-up and pack-down times, and the rain plan for every outdoor space.
journey.reaction: A clear list of what gets checked, and by whom. That's what I want: someone accountable. I notice access for elderly guests isn't on the list, though.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms capacity, exclusive use, curfew and minimum nights in writing for any Elounda venue on your shortlist.
journey.reaction: Fine the first time. By the fourth or fifth time this same sentence comes round after a section, I start skimming past it.

journey.quote: Adults only is a decision, not a detail. If nieces, nephews or godchildren are on the list, this one is out.
journey.reaction: Straight to the point. Saves us a pointless argument about my sister's grandchildren.

journey.quote: The largest figures are outdoor ones, so plan a wet-weather fallback around the indoor number for the space you choose.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the sort of thing a planner should spot before we're standing in the rain.

journey.quote: The practical details are covered: a private air-conditioned dressing room, an accessible WC, a 4.5 m by 4.5 m dance floor, private parking and an emergency generator.
journey.reaction: Again, the only venue that mentions access at all is the hilltop garden with no rooms. 'Hilltop' worries me too. For every resort I still don't know if Mum's walking frame can get from her room to the chapel.

journey.section: Getting to Crete for your wedding
journey.quote: Booking guests into the wrong airport is the costliest mistake on Crete. Minos Beach and Minos Palace both put Chania Airport about three hours away.
journey.reaction: Three hours in a car after flying from Melbourne would finish my mother off. I'm marking this for my husband, he books the flights.

journey.section: Getting to Crete for your wedding
journey.quote: For a guest list, that means one booked coach per flight wave rather than a taxi queue.
journey.reaction: Sensible. I don't want eighty relatives haggling with taxi drivers at midnight.

journey.quote: None of this rules out a summer wedding. It means shade for the ceremony, an indoor fallback for every outdoor space, and travel insurance that every guest has read.
journey.reaction: Honest about wildfires, heat and earthquakes without frightening me off. The ceremony-time table is useful. I'd like to know what kind of insurance cover older guests actually need, but at least it's raised.

journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so ask whether you need one, where to get it, and whether it needs an apostille.
journey.reaction: This paragraph is heavy going. Acronyms and two long sentences. I had to read it twice, and I still don't know who actually sorts the paperwork for us.

journey.quote: It states that the marriage must then be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days.
journey.reaction: Useful to know there's a second step after the day. The tip to keep a weekday free is the kind of thing I'd never have thought of.

journey.section: Shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, fee in writing. That's what I need. I'd still want a phone call with that person before a cent goes anywhere.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have level paths, lifts or few steps between rooms, chapel and reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
Who reads the venue contract if it is in Greek and priced in euros, and how is the venue deposit held?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Crete time?
Is the first step a phone conversation with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked or paid?
What travel or medical insurance should older guests have for a summer wedding on Crete?
Who actually prepares and lodges the legal paperwork: the venue, the Wedded Advisor or us?
would_share_with: My husband, with the airport section and the 'three hours from Chania' line marked
My daughter, with the adults-only note on Minos Palace and the capacity figures
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the heat, ceremony-time table and insurance line

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
cta_reaction.why: One named person, AUD quotes and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if it said plainly that a real person rings me first, before anything is booked, and that they can tell me which venues suit my mother's mobility.

top_3_changes: Add access to the 'Not published' lines (or the list of things the Wedded Advisor confirms in writing): level paths, lifts and steps between rooms, ceremony and reception, for guests with limited mobility.
Break the CNI paragraph in the legal section into shorter sentences or a short list, and say who handles the paperwork in practice.

Vary or trim the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms ... in writing' line after each area so it lands harder once, and say in the closing section that the first step is a phone conversation before anything is booked.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing lines and unprinted prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; turn_offs_found empty because no persona turn-off was genuinely triggered

open_questions.question: Venue accessibility for elderly guests is again this persona's main content gap (only Sea View mentions an accessible WC). Deposit protection, contract language and on-the-day contact are business details and deferred. Treat accessibility as should-fix?

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
